subject: Hearthwell initial hosting fit: residency constraints, air-gap needs and next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Priya Raman <priya.raman@hearthwellpharm.com>, Mark Eastman <mark.e@hearthwellpharm.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 May 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hearthwell initial hosting fit: residency constraints, air-gap needs and next steps

Hi Priya / Mark — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap so we have shared understanding and clear next steps. I kept this intentionally short; please flag anything I missed.

What we heard (pain / drivers)
- Regulatory residency: R&D dataset copies for investigational studies must remain within the US and cannot be replicated cross-region; retention policies vary by dataset.
- Air-gap requirement for "Tier A" clinical models: controls must prevent inbound internet access from production model hosts; onboarding will require an isolated VPC and explicit egress gating.
- Controlled export: any model artifacts containing derivations of controlled substance manufacturing data cannot leave approved networks or be logged to third-party telemetry.
- Key management & audits: customer-managed KMS/HSM preferred; audit logs required for training/eval runs for 3 years.

Technical constraints you mentioned
- No public IPs on inference hosts; all outbound must go through a company-managed NAT with strict ACLs.
- No persistent shared storage for model weights in public cloud buckets; prefer local NVMe on nodes or an approved on-prem object store.
- Strict ingress: only specific CIDR blocks from your ops VPN and our provisioning address during setup.

What Redwood can offer (fit highlights)
- Private deployment (VPC or on-prem package) with customer-controlled control plane, support for bring-your-own-KMS, and optional air-gap configuration.
- Runtime supports local NVMe model payloads and restricted telemetry toggles (we can limit or aggregate logs per dataset).
- Rollout approach: phased canary in an isolated subnet, then expand; we support documented fallback to a verification-only mode.

Immediate next steps (owners)
1) Priya: share the restricted-data-matrix.xlsx mapping datasets to residency/retention policies — due Thu 5/10. (attachment placeholder)
2) Redwood (Ben): produce a short technical note describing the air-gap deployment pattern and required VPC primitives — target Fri 5/11.
3) Oliver/Procurement (Olivia): confirm whether Hearthwell prefers a monthly reserved-capacity quote or an annual contract for budgeting — we should get that by next week.
4) Jasmine: schedule a technical deep-dive (network + security) with your infra team; propose Tue 5/14 10am PT or Wed 5/15 1pm PT.

Attachments referenced: hearthwell-network-sketch.pdf (high-level sketch from today's share), restricted-data-matrix.xlsx (blank template).

If this matches your view, I'll schedule the deep-dive and Ben will attach the deployment note.

Thanks,
— Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Dr. Priya Raman <priya.raman@hearthwellpharm.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Eastman <mark.e@hearthwellpharm.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@hearthwellpharm.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 May 2028 17:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hearthwell initial hosting fit: residency constraints, air-gap needs and next steps

Thanks Jasmine — this is an accurate summary. A couple of clarifications / additions from our side:
- The retention window for certain Phase II trial derivatives is 7 years, not 3. We need that baked into any audit logging policy.
- For the air-gapped tier, we will allow a one-time outbound call to our artifact verification service during deployment; after that, network egress must be disabled.
- We will provide the dataset matrix tomorrow morning (5/8).

I accept Tue 5/14 10am PT for the technical deep-dive. Please invite our infra lead, Kevin Shaw (kevin.shaw@hearthwellpharm.com).

Priya
Dr. Priya Raman
Head of Clinical Data Platforms | Hearthwell Pharmaceuticals
priya.raman@hearthwellpharm.com

- I will draft the air-gap deployment note including: VPC design (no public IPs), provisioning window and one-time verification callback flow, KMS integration patterns, recommended NVMe layout for weights. Will attach sample config snippets.
- Security checklist to include: audit log retention mapping (3/7 year split), telemetry opt-out toggles, and proof-of-delivery for model artifacts.
- Need to confirm whether Kevin (infra lead) has any appliance-based HSMs we must integrate with or whether we can rely on AWS CloudHSM in a dedicated account.

I plan to have the doc to Jasmine by EOD Fri 5/11. If we can get the restricted-data-matrix tomorrow as Priya noted, that will let me call out the exact retention SLAs.
